name: Daily Brief Generator
command:
You are generating a daily brief for the user's Home dashboard. IMPORTANT: The brief is stored as JSON in a SQLite database. Use $JOB_DB (always set for agent jobs). ## Step 1: Ensure the briefs table exists Run this SQL via bash: ``` sqlite3 "$JOB_DB" "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS briefs (date TEXT PRIMARY KEY, brief_json TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')));" ``` Do NOT write standalone Python scripts to /tmp — they will not inherit job env vars and will fail silently. ## Step 2: Gather context Use list_jobs() to discover data sources in this workspace. For each job that may have useful data, inspect its database with: ```bash sqlite3 "$PAPR_HOME/Jobs/{jobId}/data/data.db" ".tables" ``` Then use your available tools (bash, Papr Memory, filesystem) to gather relevant context: - Calendar events (if a calendar sync job exists) - Recent conversations/memory for priorities, tasks, goals - Active jobs and their status - Scheduled meetings, deadlines, or reminders - Workspace notes: `$PAPR_HOME/workspace.md` and other markdown in `$PAPR_HOME/` ### Always consult Papr Memory for canonical facts Before populating any tracker, OKR, ARR, fundraising, or company-progress section, run `search_agent_memory` with queries like: - "canonical company facts current" - "fundraising structure" - "ARR revenue current" - "OKR targets this quarter" Memory is the user's source of truth — do NOT invent numbers or rely on stale snapshots from other job databases. If memory is silent on a topic, omit the metric or mark it as unknown rather than guessing. ### Pull live financial data when keys are available If the user has connected service API keys (exposed as env vars), prefer live data over cached values: - `$STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` → compute ARR from active subscriptions (annualized MRR) - `$HUBSPOT_API_KEY`, `$SALESFORCE_*` → pull pipeline/deal data - `$GITHUB_TOKEN` → pull repo/PR status If you cannot access specific services, create a helpful brief based on whatever context IS available. Never fabricate numbers. ## Step 3: Generate the brief JSON Create a JSON object with this EXACT structure (the dashboard renders these types): ```json { "hero": { "date": "Wednesday, April 16, 2026", "title": "Your Daily Brief", "subtitle": "Here's what matters today", "stats": [{"value": "3", "label": "meetings"}, {"value": "5", "label": "priorities"}, {"value": "2", "label": "alerts"}] }, "sections": [ { "type": "priorities", "title": "Today's Priorities", "items": [{"rank": 1, "title": "Priority title", "why": "Why this matters"}] }, { "type": "timeline", "title": "Today's Schedule", "items": [{"time": "9:00 AM", "title": "Meeting name", "tags": ["internal"], "detail": {"Agenda": "Discussion points", "Prep": "What to prepare"}}] }, { "type": "alerts", "title": "Alerts & Reminders", "items": [{"severity": "medium", "message": "Alert message", "action": "Suggested action"}] }, { "type": "freeform", "title": "Daily Insight", "content": "

A helpful insight or summary paragraph.

" } ] } ``` Optional section types: "tracker" (OKR progress), "intel" (research notes). ## Step 4: Save to database Use today's date as the key (YYYY-MM-DD). UPSERT so re-runs update rather than duplicate: ```bash sqlite3 "$JOB_DB" "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO briefs (date, brief_json, created_at) VALUES ('$(date +%Y-%m-%d)', '', datetime('now'));" ``` Escape single quotes in JSON as ''. ## Step 5: Verify the save Confirm the row exists before finishing: ```bash sqlite3 "$JOB_DB" "SELECT date, length(brief_json) FROM briefs WHERE date='$(date +%Y-%m-%d)';" ``` If the SELECT returns no row, the save failed — retry with bash/sqlite3 directly. Do NOT report success unless verification passes. ## Rules - PASSIVE ONLY: use whatever data exists; do not ask the user to install tools mid-run - Always include at least: hero + priorities + one other section - Keep items concise (dashboard is for quick scanning) - Use real data when available; helpful placeholders when not - severity: "high", "medium", "low", "info"; timeline tags: "internal", "external", "milestone"
